new_statements.quote: Generalizing across Mixtec varieties, Josserand (1983:180) defines the couplet as "composed of two syllables and carrying stress on the first of these two," implying that all Mixtec varieties have the same stress behavior. [...] In sum, default stress on the first syllable of the couplet is widely reported in Mixtec. (Carroll 2015:86) -- Stress on the penultimate syllable or vowel of the couplet [...] is reported in the vast majority of Mixtec descriptions [...], and Josserand 1983:180 posits stress on the penult syllable of the couplet for Proto-Mixtec. (Penner 2019:91-92)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the first syllable of the disyllabic (bimoraic) root 'couplet', i.e. the penultimate syllable of the bare root; prefixes and enclitics do not carry the default stress. This is Josserand's family-wide (Proto-Mixtec) generalization from her survey; Chazumba and Cosoltepec are survey points but no Chazumba-specific stress data or statement exists.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned for Chazumba or in the family-wide statement.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Chazumba. Carroll notes that in some varieties (Silacayoapan, Alacatlatzala) a vocalic enclitic interacts with stress placement; not reported for Northern Baja.
new_statements.domain_note: Word/root level (the couplet = disyllabic root, citation forms of Josserand's 188-item survey wordlists). Second-hand and generic: Josserand's own p. 180 text was not opened; her Chazumba wordlist is 0% tone-marked and carries no phonological description.
new_statements.identity_note: chaz1235 [xtb] = Santiago Chazumba and Cosoltepec (Oaxaca) plus Tequixtepec, Zapotitlan, Petlalcingo and Totoltepec (Ethnologue 2019); INALI variant 'da'an davi (de la frontera Puebla-Oaxaca)' (CLIN 2008) covers this plus mit. ELP 'Northern Baja Mixtec' (10534) merges chaz1235 with chig1239 Chigmecatitlan [mii] and sout3001 Southern Puebla / Acatlan / Xayacatlan [mit], which is why Glottolog lists Acatlan, Chigmecatitlan and Xayacatlan de Bravo as alternative names on the chaz1235 page. The only first-hand phonology in the group (Pike & Wistrand 1974 'Acatlan Mixtec') and the SIL dictionary/word list are for Xayacatlan/Acatlan/Tonahuixtla = sout3001 [mit], not chaz1235. The stress statement quoted here is Josserand's family-wide (Proto-Mixtec) generalization, with Chazumba and Cosoltepec among her survey towns.
